eli: Heads-up — we started a gradual rollout with CUDA 13.1-driver patch to canary and seeing a surprising uptick in small-batch p99 (~+18-22%) for seq=32 workloads on several canaries. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/perf/rolling?run=canary
marc: CI smallbatch perf job on main also failed this morning: https://ci.redwood/job/perf-smallbatch/1234 — p99 +20% vs baseline
ci-bot: CI: nightly/perf-smallbatch failed on job 1234 — test smallbatch-32 regression detected (p99 +19%). See logs: https://ci.redwood/job/perf-smallbatch/1234/console
tara: Can we pause the rollout? Canaries still at ~30% traffic but let's stop the ramp until we know more.
ops-bot: Paused canary ramp for CUDA 13.1-driver patch in us-west-2. Routing rule toggled to hold state.
shweta: I spun up a canary VM and ran a quick nvprof/NSight profile. Kernel selection flipped from cublasLt matmul to our matmul_v2_custom path after the driver bump. Quick nvprof snippet:
```
# before (old driver)
<matmul> cublasLtMatmul  time=1.2ms  calls=120
# after (cuda13.1 canary)
<matmul> matmul_v2_custom  time=1.7ms  calls=120
```
L2/SM metrics look worse for the custom kernel on low-batch workloads.
samir: OK, can we bisect to a particular commit? Or is this purely driver-induced?
eli: Started a local bisect across recent runtime merges — initial suspect is commit 9f3a7b2 (PR #987) "scheduler: prefer matmul-v2 when occupancy>60%" which bumped the matmul priority heuristic. With that heuristic + the new driver PTX/layout, the selector is preferring our custom kernel for tiny batches.
marc: PR #987 landed in runtime 2.18 — it nudges selection weights so matmul_v2 gets chosen more often for GPUs with >60% occupancy. That change was fine on older drivers because cublasLt won for small batches; after 13.1 the relative performance shifts.
shweta: More profiling evidence — full snippet from NSight showing memory metrics and occupancy: 
```
Kernel: matmul_v2_custom
Duration: 1.72 ms
SM Occupancy: 42%
L2 Hit Rate: 64% -> (bad for small batches)

Kernel: cublasLtMatmul
Duration: 1.18 ms
SM Occupancy: 78%
L2 Hit Rate: 81% -> (better locality)
```
It looks like the custom kernel suffers on tiny batch sizes because of worse cache utilization under the new driver codegen.
tara: Two immediate remediation options: 1) revert PR #987 (quick but coarse), or 2) tweak heuristic to force cublasLt for batch<=8 and seq<=64 (targeted). Which is faster to validate?
samir: Revert is fastest to get back to baseline while we investigate the root cause, then we can reintroduce a smarter heuristic with a driver-aware selector.
ci-bot: Perf run for revert branch (revert-9f3a7b2) triggered: https://ci.redwood/job/perf-smallbatch/1250 — queued.
ops-bot: Hold internal rollout until that perf run completes and shows no regressions.
deploy-bot: Rolling config change to route canary traffic to scheduler=legacy-priority on 3/4 canary nodes now.
eli: After switching scheduler to legacy-priority on canaries p99 dropped back to baseline within 5 minutes. Continuing to monitor for 15m window.
marc: Post-mortem action items: add driver x kernel selection matrix to nightly perf, expand perf-smallbatch matrix to include seq/batch combos, and add an automated guard to disallow scheduler heuristic changes without cross-driver perf tests.
shweta: I'll open the revert PR and the follow-up feature PR to add driver-aware selection tests.
tara: Thanks — leaving the paused rollout in place until CI-green + 30m stable on canaries.
ci-bot: Perf run 1250 completed: smallbatch-32 p99 within baseline +/-1% on revert branch.
ops-bot: Revert candidate validated by CI. Proceeding with full rollback once infra run completes.
deploy-bot: Full rollback executed: runtime scheduler reverted in prod, rollout paused. Monitoring continues.
eli: Great job triaging everyone. Follow-ups: (1) add targeted unit perf tests for smallbatch->kernel mapping, (2) schedule a deep dive with Nvidia if driver-codegen differences persist.
